newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goodman no comment on Burns talk.
newsitem.headline: Goodman no comment on Burns talk.

text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Thursday that it would not comment on a report in The Australian newspaper that it was a possible bidder for fellow food company Burns Philp and Co, but repeated earlier comments that acquisitions were part of its growth strategy.
"We are not going to comment on that article," a Goodman spokesman told Reuters.
"But we are always looking at a range of options," he said.
The newspaper article said Goodman executives and the company's advisers would prefer to buy Burns Philp's profitable yeast business but a full takeover was another alternative.

"Executives and advisers to the baking, cereal foods and margarines group have been burning the midnight oil since Monday when Burns Philp ditched a core element of its global strategy by putting its profitless European and U.S. herb and spice business up for sale," the newspaper said.

The divestment announcement and the resignation of Burns Philp managing director Ian Clack surprised traders and investors who initially sent the shares higher. But the stock has fallen back sharply on speculation that the A$800 million herb and spice operations will be sold for less than book value.
The Goodman spokesman would not say if there was any synergy with Burns Philp.
"We have talked about the fact that we were going to focus on building up core assets in Australasia (Australia and New zealand)," the spokesman said.

"We would do that through organic growth and through acquisitions. And we indicated (around the time of the half year profit statement in early March) that we were in no hurry to make those acquisitions."
Goodman chief executive David Hearn said at the time that the company would decide within 12 months how to spend the A$300 million raised from the sale of its European milling and baking business.
Burns Philp shares were four cents lower at A$1.75 at noon (0200 GMT), giving the company a market capitalisation of A$917.6 million.
Its spice business rival in the United States, McCormick and Co Inc, said earlier this week it was considering a number of options following the Burns Philp announcement. It did not elaborate.
Analysts have said other potential buyers of the spice operations were Campbell Soup Co, Conagra Inc and CPC International Inc.
